Astra.Gravity Well: WHEN: Use on common hold spots (default plant corners, behind boxes) right as your team swings, or to punish a defuse tap. WHY: Pulls enemies off cover, breaks crosshair placement, and combos with damage/CC for guaranteed value. HOW: Star first, then trigger when footsteps/defuse audio starts; coordinate with nade/molly/shock to hit the pulled zone. BETTER: Don’t gravity-well without follow-up; avoid pulling enemies *into* safety for them; track enemy util that can break your combo (dash/TP) and time it when escapes are down.
Astra.Nova Pulse: WHEN: Use off-contact to stop a fast hit (entry choke) or mid-round to win an info fight (stun common close corners before you swing). WHY: Disrupts timing, forces wide/frozen entries, and sets up easy trades. HOW: Place the star early, trigger as enemies commit (listen for steps/utility), then swing on the concussed window with a teammate. BETTER: Don’t fire it “on cooldown”—wait for confirmed pressure; avoid stunning empty space; pair with a peek or teammate flash so the stun converts into a kill.
Astra.Nebula / Dissipate: WHEN: Use to deny a key sightline during executes, to stall a retake pinch, or to safely cross/plant. WHY: Breaks enemy vision, forces them to waste util or reposition, and buys seconds for rotations. HOW: Smoke the angle that matters most (entry lane or defender anchor sight), then re-smoke as it fades by recalling/placing. BETTER: Don’t triple-smoke the same lane; smoke where your team can actually take space; avoid “late” smokes after teammates are already exposed; recall (Dissipate) to fake pressure and reposition your smoke timing.
Astra.Cosmic Divide: WHEN: Use to split a site/retake (cut off Operator lanes), secure a safe plant, or isolate a 2v2 into two 1v1s. WHY: Removes long-range threat and creates “your rules” fights. HOW: Place the wall so your team owns one side (plant + post-plant angles) while denying the strongest defender sightline; immediately take space to prevent them walking through for free. BETTER: Don’t wall too shallow (they walk around); don’t wall and then hesitate—use the timing to plant or pinch; communicate which side is “ours” so teammates don’t drift into no-man’s land.

Breach.Aftershock: WHEN: Clear tight corners (behind default boxes) or force a defender off a strong hold right before entry/retake. WHY: Converts “unchecked” space into safe space by punishing camping. HOW: Aim through the wall at the exact pocket defenders play; fire as your duelist is ready to swing so the defender must move into your crosshair. BETTER: Don’t Aftershock randomly—use info (Sova dart, Cypher cam, sound) or common timings; avoid clipping teammates; don’t waste it on enemies who can easily strafe out unless it creates a favorable swing.
Breach.Flashpoint: WHEN: Start an exec, re-peek after contact, or pop-flash a teammate into a duel. WHY: Creates free kills by forcing turns or blind sprays. HOW: Pop it close to the edge of the wall for minimal reaction time; call “flashing” and swing with it (or let your teammate swing first). BETTER: Stop telegraphing with slow setups; avoid flashing your own entry; vary height/side so enemies can’t pre-turn; don’t chain flashes with no one ready to capitalize.
Breach.Fault Line: WHEN: Use to stop a rush through a chokepoint or to break a crossfire before your team swings. WHY: Concuss reduces aim control and movement, making holds fragile. HOW: Charge just enough for the lane you need; time it with your team’s step-in so concussed defenders can’t reset. BETTER: Don’t full-charge every time (gives them time to dodge); don’t concuss space your team isn’t contesting; track enemy “anti-stun” escapes (Jett dash, Chamber TP) and aim to catch the second player, not the escapist.
Breach.Rolling Thunder: WHEN: Use as the “go button” for site takes or as a retake reset when defenders are dug in. WHY: Guarantees displacement and lets your team flood space safely. HOW: Ult down the main defender lane to knock up anchors and force them off angles, then immediately hit with your team (plant or trade). BETTER: Don’t ult too early when teammates are far; avoid ulting empty site (no info); choose a line that hits the *anchor* positions and also denies rotate lanes so they can’t counter-swing instantly.

Brimstone.Stim Beacon: WHEN: Before a coordinated hit, fast rotate, or post-plant hold where your team will take multiple gunfights quickly. WHY: Faster firing/reload and movement tempo can swing trades and multi-kills. HOW: Drop it where multiple teammates will stand (entry staging or post-plant pocket) and *then* commit together. BETTER: Don’t stim only yourself unless it’s a planned solo play; avoid placing it in the open; don’t waste it after the fight already started—use it to *start* the fight on your terms.
Brimstone.Incendiary: WHEN: Deny a push through a choke, delay a defuse, or clear common close corners. WHY: Buys time, forces reposition, and punishes “stick” decisions. HOW: Bounce it to land precisely on the defuse/entry line; pair with a smoke so they can’t see the safe edge. BETTER: Don’t molly where they can simply step out and keep the same angle; save it for high-leverage timing (post-plant); communicate your molly lineup timing so teammates don’t swing while it’s still blocking your own path.
Brimstone.Sky Smoke: WHEN: Any time you need to cross, plant, or take a lane without giving Operators free shots. WHY: Blocks vision and forces defenders to guess/rotate. HOW: Smoke the two most dangerous angles first (anchor + rotate support); leave one smoke for mid-round re-hit or post-plant. BETTER: Don’t smoke too deep (gives defenders space to play inside); don’t smoke so late that your entry dies; vary patterns so opponents can’t read “A every time” from your smoke placement.
Brimstone.Orbital Strike: WHEN: Stop a plant/defuse, punish a trapped player (stun/pull), or clear a tight post-plant pocket. WHY: Forces movement and can secure the round without a direct duel. HOW: Ult on audio cue (tap defuse/plant) or on confirmed position; swing as they leave cover. BETTER: Don’t ult “hope spots” with no info; avoid ulting if teammates are about to swing into it; use it to *force* a predictable escape route you can pre-aim, not just for raw damage.

Chamber.Trademark: WHEN: Hold flank, protect a lurk, or anchor a lane while you take an aggressive first duel elsewhere. WHY: Auto-slow + info lets you rotate early and prevents silent timings. HOW: Place it in a path they must cross (not an easily wall-banged corner) and play so you can react to the trigger. BETTER: Don’t place it too close to the fight (it gets cleared instantly); update it when your team changes map control; don’t ignore the info—call it and reposition immediately.
Chamber.Headhunter: WHEN: Eco/half-buy rounds, long-range jiggle fights, or as a “finisher” after body tagging with rifles. WHY: High precision turns small advantages into kills. HOW: Use it like a pocket Sheriff—take calm, single-shot peeks; hold tight angles where head level is predictable. BETTER: Don’t spam shots and drain your economy; avoid dry wide-swings without an escape plan; pair with slow/Trademark info so you take only favorable duels.
Chamber.Rendezvous: WHEN: Take a risky first contact (Operator/angle) and instantly reposition to avoid trades. WHY: Converts one kill into safety, preserving man advantage. HOW: Anchor your teleport in a safe, non-spammable spot; peek, shoot, TP instantly on contact. BETTER: Don’t TP to a spot the enemy already cleared; avoid placing anchors that can be destroyed for free; don’t over-peek after missing—TP out and reset instead of feeding.
Chamber.Tour De Force: WHEN: Swing momentum rounds where you need a free pick or to lock a lane against a fast hit. WHY: One-shot threat plus slow field can stall whole pushes. HOW: Play a long lane, take the first shot, then reposition (TP or fallback) before they trade; coordinate so teammates hold the slowed choke. BETTER: Don’t hold the same angle every shot; avoid ulting on defense if you can’t get a safe first contact; treat it like an Operator—discipline beats highlight hunting.

Clove.Ruse: WHEN: Take sites/retakes and to cut off Operator lanes during mid-round. WHY: Vision denial that’s flexible even after death (macro value). HOW: Smoke the highest-impact lines first (entry + rotate support), then refresh smokes to keep planting/defusing safe. BETTER: Don’t smoke your own entry path; avoid panicking and smoking everything—leave gaps intentionally for your team to fight; call your smoke timing so your duelist hits the exact window.
Clove.Meddle: WHEN: To break a strong hold (common anchor corner) or stop a retake swing through a choke. WHY: Applies pressure that forces movement and denies comfortable aim duels. HOW: Toss it where defenders must either back up or fight while affected; follow immediately with a swing or teammate utility. BETTER: Don’t throw it where it hits nothing; avoid using it when your team can’t capitalize; treat it as a “move them” tool—plan the angle you’re going to gain when they reposition.
Clove.Pick-me-up: WHEN: After a frag when you expect another fight immediately (multi-kill window) or to escape after overextending. WHY: Converts a single kill into tempo and survivability. HOW: Take the orb quickly in cover, then re-peek with speed to overwhelm slow rotates. BETTER: Don’t greed the pickup in the open; if you already have numbers, sometimes *don’t* re-peek—use the buff to reposition and play crossfires instead.
Clove.Not Dead Yet: WHEN: Use as a round-swinging second life—especially when you can be traded back into cover or your team can protect you. WHY: Forces opponents to commit resources/time and can flip man disadvantages. HOW: Pop it where your teammates can immediately trade or body-block; after reviving, reposition to an unexpected angle rather than re-taking the same duel. BETTER: Don’t ult alone deep in enemy territory; avoid ulting when you’ll be instantly re-killed with no cover; communicate “protect my revive” so teammates know the plan.

Cypher.Trapwire: WHEN: Lock flanks, anchor a site, or delay a push through a chokepoint. WHY: Info + tether punishes careless entries and buys rotate time. HOW: Place at knee height across natural paths and pair with spam angles or cages; play to swing when it triggers. BETTER: Don’t place obvious wires that get pre-fired; vary placements each round; avoid stacking both wires on the same lane if you need map-wide coverage.
Cypher.Cyber Cage: WHEN: Stop a rush, isolate a duel, or create a safe cross/defuse zone. WHY: Breaks vision and manipulates timing. HOW: Cage on trigger (wire/cam info), then spam through it or swing as enemies exit; use cages to “slice” a site into manageable chunks. BETTER: Don’t cage too early (they wait it out); avoid caging with no plan to fight/escape; combine with trips so enemies are forced into predictable exits.
Cypher.Spycam: WHEN: Early round for info, mid-round to confirm rotations, or post-plant to watch defuse. WHY: Low-risk information that enables perfect setups. HOW: Place it high and off-center so it’s harder to clear; tag at the moment your team is ready to act. BETTER: Don’t tag instantly (reveals the cam); avoid putting cam in the most common pre-aim spot; after it’s spotted, reposition it next round—predictability kills value.
Cypher.Neural Theft: WHEN: Immediately after a kill in a contested area (site take/retake) when enemy positions are still valuable. WHY: Turns chaos into a map—enables instant pinch decisions. HOW: Ult and call the revealed pings fast (“two back site, one rotate”), then collapse with numbers. BETTER: Don’t ult late when they’ve already rotated; protect the corpse so you can safely ult; use the info to *move* (pinch/plant), not just to “know” and then stand still.

Deadlock.Barrier Mesh: WHEN: Stall an exec, block a retake lane, or secure a post-plant pocket. WHY: Creates temporary map geometry that forces pathing changes. HOW: Deploy to cut off the strongest defender swing route, then reposition to hold the forced choke. BETTER: Don’t place it so enemies can break it from safety; use it to *isolate* fights (2v1) not just to “block”; communicate where the wall is so teammates don’t get split.
Deadlock.Sonic Sensor: WHEN: Anchor a site or protect a lane where you expect noisy commits (steps, jumps, drops). WHY: Stun on sound turns chaotic pushes into free kills. HOW: Place it on walls near chokepoints and play an angle that sees the stunned exit. BETTER: Don’t place it where it’s easily pre-fired; avoid overlapping with teammates’ traps that give the same info; remember it’s sound-based—bait noise (jump spot) then punish the trigger.
Deadlock.GravNet: WHEN: Stop a fast entry through a choke or punish a defender holding close behind cover. WHY: Forces enemies to remove the net or fight impaired, buying time for trades. HOW: Throw it so it lands where they must move (default entry line), then swing on the “remove” animation timing. BETTER: Don’t toss it where they can back up with no consequence; coordinate with crossfire so netted targets can’t be rescued; avoid using it after the fight is already decided.
Deadlock.Annihilation: WHEN: Use to guarantee a numbers advantage on a key defender/retaker (anchor, defuser). WHY: Removes a player if they can’t be freed, forcing a desperate team response. HOW: Fire it down a predictable lane or at a trapped target; immediately hold the cocoon line with teammates. BETTER: Don’t ult with no follow-up; avoid shooting it into open space where it’s easily dodged; choose moments when the enemy team can’t safely push to break the tether.

Fade.Prowler: WHEN: Clear close corners on entry/retake or chase a hit-confirmed trail. WHY: Forces defenders to shoot (revealing position) or get nearsighted. HOW: Send it along the exact path you want to clear, then follow behind it at trade distance. BETTER: Don’t send prowler and wait—walk with it; avoid using it where it gets stuck on geometry; chain it with Haunt/Nightfall so it reliably acquires a target.
Fade.Seize: WHEN: Trap defenders in common hold spots or stop a defuse/plant attempt. WHY: Tether + decay makes targets easy to finish and prevents reposition. HOW: Throw onto the pocket behind cover, then swing with a teammate or combo with nade/molly. BETTER: Don’t throw it at max range with no timing; use info first (Haunt) so you seize the right spot; anticipate escape routes—throw where they *want* to play, not where they *were* five seconds ago.
Fade.Haunt: WHEN: Start a hit (reveal site anchors), retake to find post-plant positions, or mid-round to confirm a rotate. WHY: Info makes every duel easier and denies lurks. HOW: Place it high and off-angle so it survives longer; pop it right before your team commits so pings are actionable. BETTER: Don’t throw it where it’s instantly shot; vary lineups; if it gets destroyed immediately, treat that as info (someone is watching) and adjust your entry path.
Fade.Nightfall: WHEN: Use as the “commit” tool for site takes/retakes when you need defenders blinded and revealed. WHY: Breaks crossfires and enables safe space-taking. HOW: Ult along the lane that hits the most defenders (site + back site), then explode in with Prowlers and trades. BETTER: Don’t ult when your team can’t follow; avoid ulting too narrow (misses key angles); communicate the plan (which side you’re flooding) so everyone swings on the same timing.

Gekko.Mosh Pit: WHEN: Clear tight corners, stop a push, or deny a defuse. WHY: Forces movement and creates “no-stand” zones. HOW: Bounce it to land exactly on default plant/defuse spots; pair with Dizzy/Wingman to force awkward decisions. BETTER: Don’t throw it where it explodes harmlessly; save it for post-plant timing if your team already has site; avoid overlapping with teammate mollies unless it’s to guarantee a full denial window.
Gekko.Wingman: WHEN: Safely take space (clear a close angle), plant under pressure, or defuse with teammates covering. WHY: Offloads a high-risk objective so players can fight. HOW: Send Wingman to clear the exact corner your entry fears, then trade off its contact; for plant/defuse, smoke/flash first and hold the pinch routes. BETTER: Don’t send Wingman alone with no cover; avoid planting/defusing where Wingman is exposed to multiple angles; pick it up after to reuse—treat it like a reusable resource.
Gekko.Dizzy: WHEN: Start an exec or retake to force defenders off angles. WHY: A blind that also pressures defenders to shoot, revealing positions. HOW: Throw Dizzy above common holds so it sees over boxes; swing as it fires, aiming where blinded players must retreat. BETTER: Don’t throw it into ceilings/overhangs; avoid using it when teammates aren’t ready to swing; vary timing—sometimes hold Dizzy for the *second* contact when defenders re-peek.
Gekko.Thrash: WHEN: Use to break a site open, clear strong back-site positions, or start a retake with a guaranteed displacement. WHY: Concuss + forced movement gives your team free entry space. HOW: Drive Thrash with a clear plan: target the anchor first, then immediately call the hit and flood. BETTER: Don’t ult in the open where you’ll be killed; avoid chasing a low-value target while the anchor stays alive; coordinate so teammates swing the moment Thrash connects, not after.

Harbor.High Tide: WHEN: Execute or retake to slice the site and deny long angles. WHY: Creates a controllable “line” that forces defenders to reposition. HOW: Curve the wall to cover multiple threats (operator lane + back-site), then push behind it to claim space. BETTER: Don’t wall and then stand still—take the space it gives; avoid curving it so it blocks your team’s own crossfires; communicate the wall path so teammates know which angles are safe to cross.
Harbor.Cove: WHEN: Secure a plant/defuse or isolate a duel in a dangerous lane. WHY: Temporary cover that blocks bullets lets you complete objectives safely. HOW: Place so the edge gives you a safe exit path; combine with High Tide to block side angles. BETTER: Don’t Cove in a spot enemies can walk into and shotgun; avoid placing it when teammates need line-of-sight to trade; use it proactively (before the defuse tap) rather than reactively after you’re already pressured.
Harbor.Reckoning: WHEN: Retake or site take to flush defenders from common anchor positions. WHY: Repeated concuss zones make holding impossible and forces predictable movement. HOW: Ult to cover back-site and default; push immediately to trade stunned players. BETTER: Don’t ult too late when teammates already died; avoid ulting only the front of site; use it to force defenders into your crossfire rather than chasing them randomly.

Iso.Contingency: WHEN: Cross dangerous sightlines, isolate a lane, or create a safe plant pocket. WHY: Temporary cover turns open ground into playable space. HOW: Place it to cut off the strongest long angle first (Operator lane), then move up to a new piece of cover created by the wall. BETTER: Don’t wall too short (they see around it); avoid placing it where it blocks your team’s entry; use it in combination with flashes/smokes so enemies can’t simply spam the edge.
Iso.Undercut: WHEN: Before swinging a tight duel (close corner/short lane) or to soften a site anchor. WHY: Debuffing targets makes trades cleaner and reduces risk. HOW: Fire it to tag the most likely defender pocket, then immediately swing with your team. BETTER: Don’t throw it after the duel has already started; avoid aiming at walls that don’t let it travel into the right space; use it to set up *specific* fights (who you’re about to peek), not general “pressure.”
Iso.Double Tap: WHEN: When you expect chained fights (entry/retake) and can snowball off the first kill. WHY: Converts one kill into durability/tempo, letting you break crossfires. HOW: Activate just before contact, take a disciplined first duel, then use the advantage to push into the next angle. BETTER: Don’t pop it while rotating across the map; don’t overheat after the first kill—use cover and isolate the next fight; communicate so teammates play off your timing window.
Iso.Kill Contract: WHEN: Use to force a fair duel against a key player (site anchor, top fragger) or to safely take space in a chaotic exec. WHY: Removes external interference and converts team chaos into one decisive fight. HOW: Ult when you can immediately take the duel (close distance, known position), then play the duel patiently—win with crosshair discipline. BETTER: Don’t ult blind with no info; avoid ulting when your team needs you holding a critical lane; treat it as a win-condition—pick the right target and timing.

Jett.Cloudburst: WHEN: Quick-cross, dash entry, or to one-way a peek for a half-second. WHY: Micro-smokes break sightlines and let you reposition instantly. HOW: Toss while moving (jump/strafe) to block the exact line that threatens you, then commit to the next action (dash or swing). BETTER: Don’t throw all smokes early; save one for post-entry escape; avoid smokes that don’t actually cover the angle (practice line-of-sight); coordinate so teammates know your dash path isn’t being smoked off.
Jett.Updraft: WHEN: Take vertical off-angles, dodge utility, or combo with Blade Storm for surprise picks. WHY: Changes geometry and crosshair expectations. HOW: Use from cover, peek at apex with pre-aim, then fall back or dash after the shot. BETTER: Don’t Updraft in the open without a plan; avoid repeating the same jump spot; use it to create *one* unexpected fight, then reset—predictability gets you pre-aimed.
Jett.Tailwind: WHEN: First-contact entry, escape after taking a shot, or reposition across a dangerous lane. WHY: Converts risky peeks into low-risk info/picks. HOW: Prime dash, take the duel, then dash to a pre-selected safe spot (smoke/cover). BETTER: Don’t dash forward with no space created; avoid dashing into stacked utility; communicate your entry direction so teammates trade the space you create instead of watching you die alone.
Jett.Blade Storm: WHEN: Eco rounds, long-range fights where rifles aren’t guaranteed, or when you need mobility while staying lethal. WHY: High accuracy while moving/jumping enables aggressive picks. HOW: Take off-angles, burst for precision, and re-position between throws. BETTER: Don’t spam knives at body level; aim head-height and reset your rhythm; avoid overcommitting into crossfires—use Jett’s mobility to isolate 1v1s and disengage.

KAYO.FRAG/ment: WHEN: Clear tight corners, deny a rush, or delay defuse/plant. WHY: Multi-tick damage forces movement and punishes stationary holds. HOW: Throw to land exactly on the corner pocket or default plant line; swing when enemies are forced to exit. BETTER: Don’t throw it “somewhere on site”; use info/sound to place precisely; avoid wasting it on enemies who can back up without losing the angle; coordinate so teammates hold the forced exit path.
KAYO.FLASH/drive: WHEN: Pop-flash for entries, re-peeks, or to bail a teammate out of a duel. WHY: Creates free timings when opponents must turn. HOW: Use quick pop flashes off walls/ceilings for minimal react time; call “flashing” and swing with it. BETTER: Don’t slow-wind obvious flashes; avoid flashing behind teammates; vary pop vs high-arc to beat pre-turns; always pair with an actual swing—flashes without pressure get shrugged off.
KAYO.ZERO/point: WHEN: Start executes/retakes to disable defenders’ utility, or punish set-play comps (Sentinel stacks). WHY: Suppression removes their defensive “buttons.” HOW: Knife common anchor spots through walls; follow immediately while they’re suppressed. BETTER: Don’t knife empty space—use recon/sound/common timings; avoid knifing too early (they wait it out); call who is suppressed so your team targets the now-utilityless player.
KAYO.NULL/cmd: WHEN: Break a site hold, retake through layered utility, or force defenders off ult-dependent plays. WHY: Suppression aura + revive potential lets your team brute-force space. HOW: Pop it as you’re about to hit the choke; lead the entry so the aura covers teammates; if downed, call for a safe revive window. BETTER: Don’t ult from far away (wastes aura time); avoid ulting alone; treat it as a timing tool—hit the site during the strongest suppression window, not after it ends.

Killjoy.Nanoswarm: WHEN: Post-plant denial, stall a push, or punish enemies stuck in a choke. WHY: Hidden damage zones convert taps into panic. HOW: Pre-place on default plant/entry lines; activate on audio cue (plant/defuse/steps) while holding the exit angle. BETTER: Don’t activate instantly—wait for commitment; avoid stacking both nanos on low-value timing; protect line-of-sight so enemies can’t pre-shoot the nade spot before it’s used.
Killjoy.Alarmbot: WHEN: Flank watch or to tag an entry target for easy trades. WHY: Vulnerable debuff makes targets melt. HOW: Place it where it must path into them (not stuck on geometry), then hold a spam angle for the tag. BETTER: Don’t place it in obvious pre-fire spots; update it when map control changes; don’t ignore the trigger—call it and swing while they’re vulnerable.
Killjoy.Turret: WHEN: Hold a lane, watch flank, or support an anchor by taking first contact info. WHY: Early warning + chip damage disrupts entries. HOW: Place it to see the lane but be hard to pre-aim; play off its contact with a crossfire. BETTER: Don’t rely on turret to “hold alone”; reposition it between rounds; avoid placing it where one jiggle clears it for free—make them spend time/utility to remove it.
Killjoy.Lockdown: WHEN: Retake or secure post-plant when you can defend the device. WHY: Forces defenders out of positions or into desperate fights. HOW: Place it behind cover with teammate protection; push as the detain timer nears completion to catch forced movements. BETTER: Don’t ult where it’s easily wall-banged or rushed; avoid ulting with no map control (they destroy it instantly); call the “detain timing” so teammates swing on the panic window.

Neon.Fast Lane: WHEN: Cross open lanes for plant/entry or to split a site into safe/unsafe halves. WHY: Denies vision and lets Neon get close. HOW: Angle the walls to cover the most dangerous sightline first; slide through at the timing teammates are ready to trade. BETTER: Don’t wall so it blocks your team’s follow-up shots; avoid using it when your team isn’t committing (wastes it); communicate the path so teammates don’t get separated behind the walls.
Neon.Relay Bolt: WHEN: Entry or retake to clear close angles and break crossfires. WHY: Concuss makes holds unreliable and opens space. HOW: Bounce it to land behind cover where defenders play; chain it with your slide/teammate swing. BETTER: Don’t throw it where it stuns nobody; learn common bounce lineups; avoid throwing both bolts instantly—save one for the *second* contact when defenders re-peak.
Neon.High Gear: WHEN: Take first space, rotate fast, or pressure timing windows mid-round. WHY: Speed creates initiative and forces defender overreaction. HOW: Sprint to take a close position, then slide to dodge pre-aim and create a tradeable first contact. BETTER: Don’t sprint into unknown space with no info; avoid sliding into crossfires; use speed to *change* fights (close distance, isolate angles), not to overheat into five guns.
Neon.Overdrive: WHEN: Eco/force rounds, breaking a stacked hold, or snowballing after getting early space. WHY: High mobility DPS overwhelms slow setups. HOW: Pop it as you enter the fight, strafe aggressively, and focus one target at a time while teammates trade. BETTER: Don’t ult at long range where rifles beat you; avoid ulting with no cover/entry path; treat it as a “close-range brawl” tool—use Fast Lane/slide to get into its best range.

Omen.Paranoia: WHEN: Start an exec/retake to blind multiple angles at once. WHY: Nearsight breaks crossfires and forces defenders to guess timing. HOW: Fire it through the choke so it hits both close and back-site lanes; swing immediately off the hit. BETTER: Don’t throw it after your team already committed and died; avoid lining it into walls that block travel; call it so teammates swing on the same beat.
Omen.Dark Cover: WHEN: Deny Operators, enable crosses, or fake pressure mid-round. WHY: Flexible smoke tempo controls vision and rotations. HOW: Smoke the “highest threat” angle first, then re-smoke to maintain space; use one-ways when holding tight chokes. BETTER: Don’t smoke too shallow (gives them space) or too deep (they play inside); don’t dump all smokes early; coordinate with entries so the smoke lands before the peek.
Omen.Shrouded Step: WHEN: Reposition into off-angles, escape after contact, or create a fake by TPing audibly. WHY: Unpredictable angles win duels and draw rotations. HOW: TP from cover to cover; use smokes/paranoia to mask the audio/animation. BETTER: Don’t TP into open sightlines; avoid repeating the same “flashy” TP spot; use it for small, safe repositioning more often than high-risk hero plays.
Omen.From the Shadows: WHEN: Info-gather mid-round, fast rotate to a spike site, or reposition in late post-plant. WHY: Global pressure changes the map instantly. HOW: Ult to a safe pocket (behind cover), cancel if it’s unsafe, or complete and immediately take a new timing. BETTER: Don’t ult into cleared areas with enemies nearby; avoid ulting when your team needs your gun in the current fight; use it with a plan (pinch, lurk timing), not just to “move somewhere.”

Phoenix.Blaze: WHEN: Block a sightline to cross/plant or isolate a 1v1 on entry. WHY: Temporary wall denies vision and lets Phoenix take close fights. HOW: Curve it to cut off the strongest angle and create a safe pocket; use it to walk into space while defenders are denied. BETTER: Don’t wall yourself off from teammates’ trades; avoid putting it where defenders can walk through and surprise you; use it to *take* space, not just to “look cool.”
Phoenix.Hot Hands: WHEN: Clear corners, stall a push, or heal after taking damage. WHY: Dual-purpose: space denial + self-sustain. HOW: Throw it on the exact corner pocket or choke line; if healing, do it from cover while teammates hold. BETTER: Don’t heal in open lanes; avoid mollying space your team needs to run through; save it for post-plant denial when you already have site control.
Phoenix.Curveball: WHEN: Pop-flash around tight corners for entry or to re-peek after contact. WHY: Fast blind enables solo plays and trades. HOW: Bend it tight so it pops immediately as you swing; pre-aim the most likely head-height angle. BETTER: Don’t throw wide, slow flashes that get turned; avoid flashing teammates; mix left/right timing so defenders can’t pre-turn every time.
Phoenix.Run it Back: WHEN: First entry into a contested site or to take a high-risk duel with low downside. WHY: Guarantees info/space and can secure a plant. HOW: Ult from a safe, defendable spot; push aggressively to clear corners and force rotations; call what you see. BETTER: Don’t ult when your “return” spot can be camped; avoid ulting too far from teammates (no trades); use the ult window to accomplish an objective (clear site, get spike down), not just hunt kills.

Raze.Boom Bot: WHEN: Clear close corners on entry/retake or force a defender to reveal position by shooting it. WHY: Turns unknown space into known space. HOW: Send it along the exact path you want to clear; swing behind it to trade the defender who shoots. BETTER: Don’t send it into open space where it sees nothing; avoid using it when teammates aren’t ready to capitalize; vary timing so defenders can’t always pre-fire it for free.
Raze.Blast Pack: WHEN: Fast entry, reposition, escape, or to displace defenders from tight pockets. WHY: Mobility and disruption create unfair fights. HOW: Satchel from cover, land in an off-angle, and be ready to shoot *on landing*; double-satchel to break crosshair placement. BETTER: Don’t satchel into crossfires with no info; avoid predictable flight paths; use it to isolate 1v1s and create tradeable space for teammates, not to suicide for highlights.
Raze.Paint Shells: WHEN: Clear common hold spots, stop rushes, or deny defuse/plant. WHY: Forces movement and punishes grouping. HOW: Throw to land behind cover where defenders hide; time with teammate swings so enemies can’t simply dodge then re-peek. BETTER: Don’t nade the front of site where everyone can back up; save it for confirmed positions (drone/cam/sound); avoid wasting it early if your win condition is post-plant denial.
Raze.Showstopper: WHEN: Break a stacked site hold, punish a trapped player, or swing a round off a single pick. WHY: Instant threat forces defenders to scatter. HOW: Use movement (satchel) to close distance and reduce dodge time; aim at feet/near cover edges for splash reliability. BETTER: Don’t ult from predictable choke with no entry support; avoid firing too early at long range; choose timing when defenders are committed (utility out, trapped by smokes/walls) so they can’t simply sidestep.

Reyna.Leer: WHEN: Entry or re-peek to force defenders off angles. WHY: Breaks crossfires and creates isolated fights. HOW: Place it high/offset so it’s harder to instantly shoot; swing as it activates, focusing the nearest threat. BETTER: Don’t Leer from too far (it gets shot before it matters); avoid throwing it where teammates are blind or it blocks their line; use it to take *space*—Leer + hesitation wastes the window.
Reyna.Devour: WHEN: After a kill when you need to re-fight or stabilize HP for the next duel. WHY: Sustained presence enables multi-kills. HOW: Heal from cover while teammates hold; re-peek with full HP when advantageous. BETTER: Don’t Devour in the open; if you have numbers advantage, sometimes skip healing to reposition and hold crossfires; track soul-orb timers so you don’t greed and die for a heal.
Reyna.Dismiss: WHEN: After a kill to escape a trade, cross a dangerous lane, or reposition to an off-angle. WHY: Converts aggression into safety and resets fights. HOW: Take the kill, instantly Dismiss, and move to a new angle that punishes their chase. BETTER: Don’t Dismiss into dead ends; avoid dismissing when you should be trading with your team (numbers context matters); use it to *reposition*, not to wander and lose map impact.
Reyna.Empress: WHEN: Swing rounds where you want to chain kills, especially on attack entries or retake brawls. WHY: Faster tempo plus free Dismiss/Devour makes you hard to trade. HOW: Ult right before contact, take isolated duels, and constantly reposition after each kill. BETTER: Don’t ult when the fight is already over or you’re rotating across map; avoid taking long-range aim duels—force close, isolatable fights; communicate so teammates play off your aggression rather than trailing too far behind.

Sage.Barrier Orb: WHEN: Stop fast hits, create a safe plant pocket, or deny a retake route. WHY: Temporary map control forces utility spend or reroutes. HOW: Wall across the choke early if you expect a rush; or wall to create a “corner” your team can plant behind. BETTER: Don’t place a wall that enemies can instantly break with no cost; avoid walling off teammates; think about what angle you’re denying and what new angle you’re giving them—place to force awkward pathing.
Sage.Slow Orb: WHEN: Delay a push, isolate a duel, or stall a defuse/plant. WHY: Movement control breaks timing and makes targets easy to pre-aim. HOW: Throw it to cover the choke line *and* the exit, so they must fully commit to walking through; hold the edge for free kills. BETTER: Don’t slow empty space—use sound/info; avoid slowing your team’s own entry; save one slow for post-plant if your plan is to play time.
Sage.Healing Orb: WHEN: After winning space/contact when you can safely reset HP, or to keep your duelist/anchor alive for the next fight. WHY: Preserves numbers and pressure. HOW: Heal from cover and immediately re-position; prioritize the teammate who will take the next duel. BETTER: Don’t heal mid-fight in the open; avoid healing low-impact players over the entry/anchor; call who you’re healing so teammates know your timing (you may be briefly not trading).
Sage.Resurrection: WHEN: After you’ve secured space and can protect the revive, especially to recover a spike carrier or key ult. WHY: Converts a pick against you into neutral/advantage. HOW: Smoke/slow/wall first, then revive from cover; have a teammate hold the most likely swing. BETTER: Don’t rez in the open or mid-spray; don’t rez if the revived player will instantly die again; communicate “cover rez” and consider baiting the enemy swing into your crossfire.

Skye.Regrowth: WHEN: After a fight when you’ve secured cover and need to stabilize multiple teammates for the next hit/retake. WHY: Multi-target heal preserves round resources. HOW: Heal behind cover while teammates hold angles; prioritize players who will take first contact next. BETTER: Don’t heal in contested lanes; avoid healing when you should be trading; call “healing” so teammates know you’re briefly not swinging.
Skye.Trailblazer: WHEN: Clear close corners on entry/retake or scout a lane safely. WHY: Info + concuss converts unknown space into a free swing. HOW: Send it tight to walls so it checks corners; bite (stun) then call and swing immediately. BETTER: Don’t scout while teammates are too far to capitalize; avoid sending it into open mid where it gets shot instantly; use it to clear the *next* dangerous corner, not the one your teammate already checked.
Skye.Guiding Light: WHEN: Pop-flash for entries, isolate a defender, or re-take space after contact. WHY: Flexible flash that can be steered for multi-angle pressure. HOW: Curve it around the corner and pop it as teammates swing; vary heights to catch common anti-flash positions. BETTER: Don’t pop too early (it blinds nobody) or too late (teammates already died); avoid flashing your team; use quick “pop” timing more than long floaty flashes that defenders can hide from.
Skye.Seekers: WHEN: Retake/site take when you need to locate the last defenders or clear post-plant hiding spots. WHY: Forces defenders to shoot/reveal or get nearsighted. HOW: Ult, track which seeker targets which lane, then pinch the revealed side with teammates. BETTER: Don’t ult when you already know all positions; avoid ulting with no ability to follow (too far away); treat seeker paths as a “map ping” and move decisively rather than hesitating.

Sova.Owl Drone: WHEN: Clear an entry lane, confirm site anchor positions, or set up shock/dart lineups safely. WHY: Reliable info without risking a body. HOW: Drone from cover, tag high-value targets (anchor/Operator), and call exact positions for your entry. BETTER: Don’t drone with teammates idle behind you—sync the hit; avoid droning too deep and losing it instantly; prioritize tagging the player who matters most to break the defense, not chasing a random lurker.
Sova.Shock Bolt: WHEN: Punish common holds, clear utility (where applicable), or deny defuse/plant. WHY: Forced movement and chip damage convert taps into wins. HOW: Use bounce lineups to land exactly on default plant/defuse spots; time with audio cues. BETTER: Don’t fire shocks blindly early; save at least one for post-plant if that’s your win condition; communicate so teammates swing when the target is forced off cover.
Sova.Recon Bolt: WHEN: Start executes/retakes or mid-round to confirm map control. WHY: Info turns guesses into plans. HOW: Dart high, off-angle, and behind cover so it survives; pop it when your team can immediately act on the scans. BETTER: Don’t dart the most obvious wall every round; avoid darting when teammates can’t capitalize; if it gets insta-shot, treat it as info (someone is watching) and adjust your entry path or timing.
Sova.Hunter's Fury: WHEN: Stop plant/defuse, punish stuck targets (stun/tether), or secure kills after recon reveals. WHY: Long-range kill/deny tool that also clears space. HOW: Ult immediately off recon tag/scan and track likely dodge paths; coordinate with teammate slows/stuns for guaranteed hits. BETTER: Don’t ult with no info; avoid “sniping” randomly while the spike is being planted/defused elsewhere; use the first beam to force movement, the second to punish the path, and the third to confirm.

Tejo.Stealth Drone: WHEN: Early round to take safe map control, or before a hit to confirm anchor positions without risking a body. WHY: Suppress + reveal turns defender setups into predictable, utility-less fights. HOW: Pilot through safe routes, pulse when you’re near likely defender pockets, then call suppressed targets so your team hits the weakened side. BETTER: Don’t drone too deep with no follow-up; avoid pulsing empty lanes—use timing (when defenders can’t rotate away); keep the drone path low-risk so you don’t lose it instantly to pre-fire.
Tejo.Special Delivery: WHEN: Clear close corners, punish a defender holding tight behind cover, or interrupt a push through a choke. WHY: Concuss forces missed shots and breaks coordinated swings. HOW: Stick it to the corner surface they’re tucked behind; alt-fire for a controlled bounce to land precisely; swing on the concuss timing with a teammate. BETTER: Don’t throw it into open space where they sidestep; avoid using it without a planned peek; prioritize concussing the *anchor* or first-contact player to collapse the hold.
Tejo.Guided Salvo: WHEN: Start executes to flush defenders off default angles, or mid-round to deny a held pocket so your team can walk in. WHY: Forces reposition and creates timing windows for entry. HOW: Mark targets where defenders must stand (behind default, back-site cubbies), launch, then hit the site *as the detonations land* so they can’t re-peek. BETTER: Don’t salvo after teammates already swung; avoid targeting low-impact space; stagger targets to herd defenders into a predictable escape route your team is holding.
Tejo.Armageddon: WHEN: Round-swinging commit tool: clear a lane during exec, deny a defuse line, or split a retake by forcing everyone off a corridor. WHY: Sustained lethal pressure turns strong holds into forced retreats. HOW: Draw the strike path to cut through anchor + rotate route; call the path, then take space immediately while enemies are displaced. BETTER: Don’t ult when your team can’t capitalize; avoid paths that leave defenders safe behind hard cover the whole time; use it to force a *predictable* exit that your teammates can pre-aim.

Veto.Crosscut: WHEN: Take first contact and instantly reposition (or escape) while still anchoring a lane. WHY: Teleport anchor lets you play aggressive angles without being traded. HOW: Place the vortex in a safe pocket; fight from a forward angle; when pressured, activate while looking at the vortex to snap back and reset. BETTER: Don’t place vortex where it’s easily destroyed/cleared; avoid using it as a panic button into unsafe space; plan the exit so you re-appear behind cover with a teammate ready to trade.
Veto.Chokehold: WHEN: Stop a rush, trap a post-plant swing path, or punish a defuse tap. WHY: Tether + deafen + decay makes targets helpless and easy to collapse on. HOW: Throw it onto the path they must cross (not a corner they can avoid); hold the trigger timing so it activates as they commit; swing while they’re tethered. BETTER: Don’t place it where they can shoot it for free before it matters; avoid using it without a teammate angle; use sound cues (steps/tap) so you trap commitment, not air.
Veto.Interceptor: WHEN: Protect a site/defuse/plant from projectile utility (grenades, flashes that bounce, thrown utility) and force gunfights. WHY: Deletes key enemy “buttons,” making their exec simpler—and easier to counter. HOW: Place it behind cover where it still covers the choke; activate right before the enemy dump-utility moment; fight while their setup fails. BETTER: Don’t place it where it’s instantly shot; avoid activating too early (they wait it out); reposition between rounds so opponents can’t pre-clear it on autopilot.
Veto.Evolution: WHEN: Use to win a decisive brawl—retake push, hold vs flood, or to convert a man-disadvantage into a duel-heavy round. WHY: Combat stim + regen + immunity to debuffs lets you take fights others can’t. HOW: Pop as contact starts, take space aggressively with teammates trading, and use the regen window to keep pressuring. BETTER: Don’t ult while rotating (waste time); avoid isolating yourself—your buff is strongest when teammates trade behind you; use it to *force* fights, not hide and wait.

Viper.Snake Bite: WHEN: Post-plant defuse denial, clear common close corners, or punish rushes through chokes. WHY: Vulnerable + damage makes targets easy to finish and forces reposition. HOW: Line up to land on default defuse/plant spots; combine with smoke so they can’t see the safe edge. BETTER: Don’t molly where they can simply step out and keep the same angle; save it for high-leverage timing (tap/half); communicate lineup timing so teammates hold the forced exit routes.
Viper.Poison Cloud: WHEN: One-way a choke, block a key sightline for plant/defuse, or fake pressure by toggling. WHY: Vision denial with flexible fuel timing. HOW: Place on a powerful angle (choke mouth or default plant cover), toggle as teammates cross/plant, then re-toggle for post-plant. BETTER: Don’t leave it up draining fuel when no one is using it; avoid tossing it where it’s easily destroyed; learn one-way placements that create unfair fights rather than just “a smoke.”
Viper.Toxic Screen: WHEN: Execute to split a site, cut rotations, or enable safe crosses. WHY: Reshapes the map and forces defenders into predictable gaps. HOW: Set the wall to cover the strongest defender line and isolate the anchor; raise it as your team commits, then take the space behind it. BETTER: Don’t wall where it blocks your own team’s post-plant sightlines; avoid raising it too early (wastes fuel); coordinate so teammates know which side of the wall is “safe” to push.
Viper.Viper's Pit: WHEN: Lock down a planted spike site or defend a critical area in late-round. WHY: Massive vision control + decay turns fights into Viper-favored close duels. HOW: Ult on or near the spike so you can play the objective; reposition constantly inside the pit and take short, isolatable fights. BETTER: Don’t ult where enemies can hold you from outside with spam; avoid staying predictable (same corner); use the pit to play time—don’t chase kills out of your advantage zone.

Vyse.Razorvine: WHEN: Stall a choke, protect spike post-plant, or punish fast entries that must cross a lane. WHY: Slow + damage makes pushes expensive and delays timings. HOW: Place it in a path they must traverse (not a corner they can bypass), then activate as they commit so they can’t pre-shoot and wait it out. BETTER: Don’t activate instantly—wait for footsteps/utility; avoid placing it where it’s easily cleared from safety; coordinate so teammates hold the slowed exit path for easy trades.
Vyse.Shear: WHEN: Trap a common entry/retake route to isolate the first player in. WHY: A temporary indestructible wall splits teams and forces bad spacing. HOW: Place the hidden trap where the first contact usually crosses; when it triggers, focus fire the isolated player before the rest can help. BETTER: Don’t place it in obvious pre-clear spots; vary lanes each round; don’t over-swing through your own wall—use it to create a controlled 2v1, not a chaotic fight.
Vyse.Arc Rose: WHEN: Hold a site as an anti-rush blind, or set it for retake timing where enemies must look into it. WHY: Punishes line-of-sight and forces turns, breaking crossfires. HOW: Place it stealthed on a surface that “sees” the choke; activate when you hear commitment so multiple enemies get hit; pick it up and redeploy if the fight shifts. BETTER: Don’t trigger it too early (they hide); avoid placing it where it’s instantly shot; communicate activation so teammates swing with the blind window.
Vyse.Steel Garden: WHEN: Retake/execute when enemy rifles and utility-heavy holds are the main threat. WHY: Jamming primary weapons forces awkward swaps and breaks defender firepower timing. HOW: Pop it as you enter the key lane so the jam hits the cluster; swing immediately while they’re disrupted. BETTER: Don’t ult from far away where the windup ends before contact; avoid ulting on a single isolated player; use it to break a stacked hold or to stop a coordinated retake push.

Waylay.Saturate: WHEN: Entry/retake to soften a close hold or stop a fast swing through a choke. WHY: Hinder (move + weapon slow) makes defenders easy to swing and prevents clean trades. HOW: Throw it to land at the defender’s feet behind common cover; swing while they’re hindered so their strafe/aim reset is punished. BETTER: Don’t throw it where it hits empty ground; save it for the *moment of contact* (sound cues); pair with your dash so you arrive as they’re slowed.
Waylay.Lightspeed: WHEN: Break an Operator lane, entry off a flash, or rapidly reposition after first contact. WHY: Double-dash tempo creates unfair timing windows. HOW: First dash to cross danger, second dash to hit an off-angle or close distance; keep crosshair ready to shoot immediately after movement. BETTER: Don’t dash into crossfires with no info; avoid repeating the same dash line; coordinate so teammates trade the space you create—movement without follow-up just feeds.
Waylay.Refract: WHEN: Take a risky duel and then safely reset, or bait utility/peeks during entries and post-plant. WHY: “Anchor point” return denies trades and wastes enemy time. HOW: Place the beacon before you swing; fight forward, then reactivate to snap back when pressured; use it to take space that would normally be untradeable. BETTER: Don’t place the beacon in a spot enemies can hold/clear; avoid reactivating too late (you die mid-escape); plan the return spot so you can immediately re-peek from a new angle.
Waylay.Convergent Paths: WHEN: Start a site take/retake to carve out a safe zone and force defenders off angles. WHY: Large-area Hinder pressure breaks setups and enables your team to flood. HOW: Ult along the lane that hits anchor + back-site pockets, then push with the expanding zone so defenders can’t comfortably hold. BETTER: Don’t ult when teammates can’t follow; avoid aiming it too narrow; treat it as a “space maker”—call where you’re pushing so the team collapses together.

Yoru.Fakeout: WHEN: Fake a hit, force a rotate, or create a distraction during a pinch. WHY: Baits crosshair placement and reveals reactions (shots/utility). HOW: Send it through a common entry line, then swing a different angle or follow behind it to punish the pre-aim. BETTER: Don’t fakeout with no plan—pair it with a timing (lurker pinch, Gatecrash); avoid repeating identical fakes; watch for enemies who stop shooting decoys and adjust by mixing real contact.
Yoru.Blindside: WHEN: Pop-flash around corners for entry, isolate a 1v1, or re-peek off contact. WHY: Fast flash punishes static holds. HOW: Bounce it off a nearby surface to pop immediately; swing with tight crosshair placement and commit to the duel. BETTER: Don’t throw predictable long bounces that give time to turn; avoid flashing teammates behind you; vary bounce geometry so defenders can’t pre-turn consistently.
Yoru.Gatecrash: WHEN: Set up fast rotates, post-plant reposition, or a delayed lurk timing. WHY: Teleport creates instant angle changes and breaks reads. HOW: Place the tether early to cover future options; teleport during enemy noise/utility to mask audio; take an off-angle immediately after TP. BETTER: Don’t TP into uncleared space; avoid leaving tether in obvious spots that get destroyed; use it with a purpose (pinch, escape) rather than random teleporting.
Yoru.Dimensional Drift: WHEN: Scout site setups safely, set up a guaranteed flank timing, or dodge a dangerous retake choke. WHY: Info without dying + reposition threat. HOW: Ult to check anchor positions, call everything, then exit behind cover or behind enemies for a coordinated pinch. BETTER: Don’t exit in the open; avoid using it when your team needs your gun in the current fight; treat the exit as the real play—plan where you’ll appear and how teammates will capitalize.
